description: Detailed setup of a character's situation-overview pose: UI art, animation rows, shikigami montages and parallel per-weapon attachment/animation settings for ally and enemy variants.

ID.technical: FName key in SituationOverviewPoseDataTables (DTM +0xAE0). Reached from SituationOverview.Id_SituationOverviewPose and from Item.VariableId for EGameItemType::SituationOverviewPose; the latter path checks None first. The tile widget also uses the id to find the Item row and to compare against saved/selected pose settings.

Id_CustomizeLabelText.simple: Apparently a localization id for the customization pose label.
Id_CustomizeLabelText.technical: Serialized FName (row +0x10); exported values look like ITM_SITUATION_OVERVIEW_POSE_01_<character>. No read of this property exists in the available Source/ or Plugins/ tree, so its consumer and exact presentation are unresolved. The limit is lack of an identified consumer, not proof that no shipped UI uses it.

ImageFileName.simple: Full-size pose item icon texture name.
ImageFileName.technical: FName (row +0x18). GameItemIconWidget selects it for EGameItemType::SituationOverviewPose when bShowThumbnail is false and dynamically requests the texture; GameItem_GetItemImageFileName returns it for the item type. NAME_None therefore yields no icon. Exported name pattern: T_UI_Item_SituationOverviewPose_*.

ThumbnailImageFileName.simple: Thumbnail pose item icon texture name.
ThumbnailImageFileName.technical: FName (row +0x20). Selected by GameItemIconWidget when bShowThumbnail is true, and returned by GameItem_GetItemThumbnailFileName for the same item type; passed to SetThumbnail/RequestTexture. Exported name pattern: T_UI_ItemThumbnail_SituationOverviewPose_*.

Id_CharacterAnimation_Ally.simple: CharacterAnimation row used for the ally-side pose.
Id_CharacterAnimation_Ally.technical: FName; chosen when the capture type is VsAlly. Resolved in CharacterAnimationDataTables (DTM +0x4A0); every non-None key of that animation row becomes a keyed montage file in the capture's animation map, and the first file is loaded for Idle playback. A missing row returns an empty map / aborts the capture.

Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation_Ally.simple: ShikigamiAnimation row used for the ally-side pose.
Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation_Ally.technical: FName; resolved in ShikigamiAnimationDataTables (DTM +0x6E0) for VsAlly captures. Its keyed files map to montage loaders, and FileName[0] is used when playing the shikigami idle montage on attached shikigami. Missing row yields no shikigami animation.

Id_AnimationWeapon_Ally.simple: Weapon ids used by the ally-side pose.
Id_AnimationWeapon_Ally.technical: TArray<FName> (four slots in the export), parallel to WeaponSocketName_Ally / WeaponAnimationName_Ally / bVariationWeapon_Ally. None entries are skipped. Used to hide character-weapons not listed here, override sockets for listed ones, spawn pose-only weapons when bVariationWeapon is false, preload Weapon.FileName_BP, and find the matching attached weapon montage by case-insensitive prefix.

WeaponSocketName_Ally.simple: Socket names for ally-side pose weapons.
WeaponSocketName_Ally.technical: TArray<FName>, same length/order as Id_AnimationWeapon_Ally. Overwrites the socket of an existing character weapon when its id is listed, and is the SpawnWeapon socket for a pose-only weapon. Exported slots are often None; the capture itself passes the value to SpawnWeapon without substituting 'root' (that substitution is only in the non-SituationOverview branch).

WeaponAnimationName_Ally.simple: Montage loader names for ally-side weapon animations.
WeaponAnimationName_Ally.technical: TArray<FName>, parallel to Id_AnimationWeapon_Ally. Added to the capture slot's AnimMontage loader names for non-None weapon ids (GetWeaponAnimationNames) and later looked up by weapon-id prefix to override the attached weapon mesh's montage.

bVariationWeapon_Ally.simple: Whether an ally-side pose weapon comes from a character variation.
bVariationWeapon_Ally.technical: TArray<bool> parallel to Id_AnimationWeapon_Ally. For a weapon id not already present in the character's weapon list, true skips spawning a pose-only copy (it is expected from the variation), false spawns it with the pose socket. It does not control the later variation-transform test, which uses CharacterWeapon.Id_Weapon.

Id_CharacterAnimation_Enemy.simple: CharacterAnimation row used for the enemy-side pose.
Id_CharacterAnimation_Enemy.technical: FName; selected for every capture type other than VsAlly. Same keyed-file mapping, montage loader preload and early-out on a missing row as the ally field.

Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation_Enemy.simple: ShikigamiAnimation row used for the enemy-side pose.
Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation_Enemy.technical: FName; selected for non-VsAlly captures, resolved in ShikigamiAnimationDataTables and used for keyed montage files and the attached-shikigami idle montage. Missing row stops shikigami animation setup.

Id_AnimationWeapon_Enemy.simple: Weapon ids used by the enemy-side pose.
Id_AnimationWeapon_Enemy.technical: TArray<FName> (four exported slots); takes the same weapon hiding/spawning, preload and prefix-matching path as the ally array whenever the capture is not VsAlly.

WeaponSocketName_Enemy.simple: Socket names for enemy-side pose weapons.
WeaponSocketName_Enemy.technical: TArray<FName> parallel to Id_AnimationWeapon_Enemy; used for the same existing-weapon override and pose-only spawn socket in non-VsAlly captures.

WeaponAnimationName_Enemy.simple: Montage loader names for enemy-side weapon animations.
WeaponAnimationName_Enemy.technical: TArray<FName> parallel to Id_AnimationWeapon_Enemy; used by GetWeaponAnimationNames and attached-weapon montage override for non-VsAlly captures.

bVariationWeapon_Enemy.simple: Whether an enemy-side pose weapon comes from a character variation.
bVariationWeapon_Enemy.technical: TArray<bool> parallel to Id_AnimationWeapon_Enemy; true prevents spawning a pose-only copy of a weapon not already carried, false spawns it using WeaponSocketName_Enemy.

notes: Ally/enemy arrays are selected by a single bAlly / CaptureType branch; the code assumes the four per-weapon arrays stay index-aligned (Source/Abrams/Private/GameCharacterCaptureActor.cpp:651-671, 1314-1326).
The row constructor is inline and leaves fields default-initialized; retail's TCppStructOps::Construct for it is inlined (Source/AbramsDataTable/Public/GameDataTableRow_SituationOverviewPose.h:59).

Export observation: 190 rows, all four weapon arrays have four slots; 16 rows have no ally ImageFileName/ThumbnailImageFileName/character animation, so those capture paths abort before playing. No localization variants or numbered shards of this table were exported.
Id_CustomizeLabelText is the only field here without an identified consumer in the available source; it is marked observed rather than given a guessed runtime effect.

Evidence is from the reconstructed C++ in Source/ (row shape/counts from the exported table); status/ records byte matches for some owner TUs, but this file does not claim a retail byte comparison for every function or exhaustive Blueprint/runtime coverage.

usages.detail: Pose-resolution helper joins Character -> SituationOverview -> SituationOverviewPose with an unchecked pose index.
Builds the capture weapon list from the CharacterWeapon variation row and the pose's weapon arrays, hiding non-listed weapons.
Preloads pose animation, shikigami and weapon assets for a capture slot.
Maps every keyed CharacterAnimation file for the ally/enemy pose into the capture's montage map.
Does the equivalent shikigami animation mapping.
Collects WeaponAnimationName_* montage names for non-None pose weapons.
Plays the pose's character/shikigami idle montages and overrides attached weapon mesh animations.
Renders the pose's full-size or thumbnail image as a SituationOverviewPose item icon.
Returns pose ImageFileName / ThumbnailImageFileName for item icon queries.
Builds the unlocked pose tile list; pose id is matched to an Item row and to saved selection state.
